references.title: NE 100 — Introduction to Neural Engineering
references.authority: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
references.notes: Curriculum baseline spanning neuroanatomy/neurophysiology, monitoring technologies, neural replacement/restoration devices, imaging, and computational approaches.

references.title: Neural Engineering, BS
references.authority: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
references.notes: Program-level baseline showing the field's integration of neuroscience, electrical and imaging systems, molecular/cellular engineering, biological interfacing, neural data science, design, regulation, and ethics.

references.title: About the BRAIN Initiative
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Authoritative current framing of neurotechnology development as a means to understand dynamic brain activity across cells and circuits and to advance research and clinical capabilities.

references.title: Neural Recording and Modulation
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Current authoritative map of recording and modulation technology, including electrical, optical, magnetic, acoustic, molecular, genetic, ASIC, adaptive-optics, and signal-processing components.

references.title: BRAIN 2025: A Scientific Vision
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Strategic baseline for large-scale monitoring, human neural technology, integrated measurement and perturbation, biocompatibility, chronic reliability, neural interfaces, theory, modeling, statistics, and translational goals.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.4 The Action Potential
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Open textbook foundation for membrane potential, ionic gradients, voltage-gated channels, action potentials, threshold, repolarization, and refractory behavior.

references.title: Neurological Devices
references.authority: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
references.notes: Current regulatory overview establishing diagnostic, neurointerventional, neurostimulation, sensory-restoration, prosthetic, safety, and market-access context.

references.title: Implanted Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) Devices for Patients with Paralysis or Amputation — Non-clinical Testing and Clinical Considerations
references.authority: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
references.notes: Authoritative translational baseline for implanted BCI nonclinical testing, IDE study design, device reliability, biocompatibility, electrical safety, wireless technology, MRI compatibility, and clinical considerations.

references.title: BRAIN 2.0 Neuroethics: Enabling and Enhancing Neuroscience Advances for Society
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Neuroethics baseline for closed-loop monitoring/stimulation and questions involving privacy, agency, identity, autonomy, consent, social context, and responsible innovation.

references.title: Brain-computer interfaces: Definitions and principles
references.authority: Jonathan R. Wolpaw, José del R. Millán, Nick F. Ramsey
references.notes: Foundational BCI definition emphasizing measurement of CNS activity and translation into artificial outputs that replace, restore, enhance, supplement, or improve natural CNS outputs.

references.title: Standards and Guidances for Neurological Devices
references.authority: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
references.notes: Current FDA entry point for neurological-device standards and guidance, including biocompatibility and other safety/effectiveness considerations.

references.title: Therapeutic Human Neuroscience Program
references.authority: National Institutes of Health — BRAIN Initiative
references.notes: Current translational program baseline for FDA-regulated invasive and noninvasive CNS technologies, including closed-loop sensing and stimulation.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.1 Basic Structure and Function of the Nervous System
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Primary L0 source for anatomical CNS/PNS divisions, sensation-integration-response, and somatic/autonomic/enteric functional organization.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 13.2 The Central Nervous System
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Foundation for the major adult brain regions and the spinal cord as both a communication pathway and an integration site.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Chapter 13 Review
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Compact source for peripheral nervous system structure, including ganglia, cranial/spinal nerves, and mixed sensory/motor fibers.

references.title: Neuroscience — Neural Systems
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Foundational systems-neuroscience map linking CNS/PNS anatomy, sensory pathways, somatic motor output, autonomic output, and distributed neural systems.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.2 Nervous Tissue
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Primary L0 source for neuron structure, major CNS/PNS glial categories, myelin, and nervous-tissue organization.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.4 The Action Potential
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Used here only for the pre-action-potential foundations: membrane selectivity, ion distributions, channels, pumps, and the resting electrical state.

references.title: Neuroscience — Channels and Transporters
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Foundational source for selective membrane permeability, ion channels, active transporters, and maintenance of ion concentration gradients.

references.title: Biology 2e — 35.1 Neurons and Glial Cells
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Independent introductory cross-check on neuron morphology, glial functions, myelination, and the cellular organization of nervous tissue.

references.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e — 12.4 The Action Potential
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Primary introductory source for membrane-voltage convention, resting membrane potential, ion gradients, leak channels, sodium-potassium pumping, and electrophysiological measurement.

references.title: Neuroscience — The Forces that Create Membrane Potentials
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Foundational source for electrochemical force balance, ion-specific equilibrium potentials, and the Nernst equation.

references.title: Neuroscience — The Ionic Basis of the Resting Membrane Potential
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for potassium-dominated resting permeability, the relationship of resting voltage to equilibrium potentials, and extracellular-potassium perturbation logic.

references.title: Basic Neurochemistry — The Ionic Hypothesis and Rules of Ionic Electricity
references.authority: Bertil Hille and William A. Catterall; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Used for the distinction between single-ion equilibrium and the multi-ion steady state of real cells, GHK permeability weighting, small charge movement, and the modest direct electrogenic contribution of the sodium-potassium pump.

references.title: Neuroscience — Voltage-Dependent Membrane Permeability
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Primary source for voltage-dependent Na and K permeability, threshold, regenerative depolarization, action-potential reconstruction, refractory dynamics, propagation, and myelination.

references.title: Neuroscience — Ion Channels Underlying Action Potentials
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for the channel-level basis of voltage-dependent conductances underlying action potentials.

references.title: Neuroscience — The Refractory Period
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for Na-channel inactivation, persistent K conductance, firing-rate limitation, and directional propagation during refractoriness.

references.title: Neuroscience — Long-Distance Signaling and Increased Conduction Velocity with Myelination
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for passive local current plus active regeneration, conduction velocity, and saltatory propagation; paired with NCBI Bookshelf NBK10921 for myelination details.

references.title: Neuroscience — Chapter 5: Synaptic Transmission
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Primary source for electrical versus chemical synapses, presynaptic Ca2+ entry, vesicular transmitter release, synaptic delay, and the overall physical chain of synaptic transmission.

references.title: Neuroscience — Excitatory and Inhibitory Postsynaptic Potentials
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for EPSP/IPSP definitions and the role of receptor-coupled channels, ionic conditions, reversal potentials, and firing threshold in determining excitation versus inhibition.

references.title: Neuroscience — Summation of Synaptic Potentials
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for spatial and temporal summation of subthreshold postsynaptic potentials and integration of excitation and inhibition across many synaptic inputs.

references.title: Neuroscience — Chapter 6: Neurotransmitters
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for neurotransmitter synthesis, vesicular packaging, release, receptor action, transmitter diversity, and clearance or degradation.

references.title: Neuroscience — Neural Circuits
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Primary source for the idea that neurons function in interconnected ensembles or circuits, the organization of synaptic connectivity, and circuit-level processing.

references.title: Neuroscience — Neural Systems
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for grouping related circuits into broader neural systems that support sensory, motor, and behavioral functions.

references.title: Neuroscience — Chapter 1: The Organization of the Nervous System
references.authority: Dale Purves et al.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for the multi-scale organization of nervous-system cell types, interconnections, circuits, and system-level physiological roles.

references.title: Introduction to Behavioral Neuroscience — 2.2 Neural Circuits
references.authority: OpenStax
references.notes: Contemporary introductory source for interconnected neural circuits, parallel processing, feedback, excitation-inhibition interactions, circuit models, and circuit-to-behavior examples.

references.title: Methods for Neural Ensemble Recordings — Defining Global Brain States Using Multielectrode Field Potential Recordings
references.authority: Shih-Chieh Lin and Damien Gervasoni; NCBI Bookshelf
references.version: Methods for Neural Ensemble Recordings, 2nd edition
references.notes: Primary source for interpreting EEG and LFP as population-level electrical field signals and for the relation between coordinated neural activity, oscillations, and field-potential recordings.

references.title: Local Field Potential Measurement
references.authority: U.S. National Library of Medicine; Medical Subject Headings (MeSH)
references.notes: Official terminology source defining intracerebral LFP measurement as extracellular potential recording generated by local electric currents around neurons.

references.title: Reference Manual on Scientific Evidence — Reference Guide on Neuroscience
references.authority: Federal Judicial Center / National Academies context; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for the neurovascular basis and seconds-scale oxygenation response underlying BOLD fMRI, emphasizing BOLD as a hemodynamic consequence rather than direct spike measurement.

references.title: Electrochemical Methods for Neuroscience — An Introduction to Electrochemical Methods in Neuroscience
references.authority: Adrian C. Michael and Laura M. Borland, eds.; NCBI Bookshelf
references.notes: Source for in-vivo neurochemical measurement, electrochemical microelectrodes, microdialysis, and the spatial-temporal-selectivity tradeoffs of chemical sensing.

references.title: The origin of extracellular fields and currents — EEG, ECoG, LFP and spikes
references.authority: György Buzsáki, Costas A. Anastassiou, and Christof Koch; Nature Reviews Neuroscience
references.notes: Biophysical source for extracellular-field generation, source superposition, distance and geometry effects, and the relation among spikes, LFP, ECoG, and EEG.

references.title: Implantable neurotechnologies: a review of integrated circuit neural amplifiers
references.authority: Kian Ann Ng, Elliot Greenwald, Yong Ping Xu, and Nitish V. Thakor; Medical & Biological Engineering & Computing
references.notes: Review source for electrode-to-amplifier neural recording, weak-signal conditioning, low-noise front ends, and practical implantable recording constraints.

references.title: Multi-Channel Neural Recording Implants: A Review
references.authority: Fereidoon Hashemi Noshahr, Morteza Nabavi, and Mohamad Sawan; Sensors
references.notes: System-level review covering neural amplifiers, ADCs, digitization, compression, noise, power, and multi-channel acquisition architecture.

references.title: Past, present and future of spike sorting techniques
references.authority: Hernan Gonzalo Rey, Carlos Pedreira, and Rodrigo Quian Quiroga; Brain Research Bulletin
references.notes: Review source for extracellular mixture interpretation, event detection and spike sorting as an inferential processing stage with validation limits.

references.title: Neural stimulation and recording electrodes
references.authority: Stuart F. Cogan; Annual Review of Biomedical Engineering
references.version: Annual Review of Biomedical Engineering 10, 275–309 (2008); DOI 10.1146/annurev.bioeng.10.061807.160518
references.notes: Foundational source for stimulation-electrode charge transfer, electrode materials, interface behavior, and stimulation safety considerations.

references.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation: a primer
references.authority: Mark Hallett; Neuron
references.notes: Review source for the TMS chain from brief high-current coil drive through magnetic stimulation and induced cortical electric fields to neural effects.

references.title: Mechanisms of deep brain stimulation
references.authority: Todd M. Herrington, Jennifer J. Cheng, and Emad N. Eskandar; Journal of Neurophysiology
references.notes: Review source for local, axonal, synaptic, oscillatory, and network-level DBS effects and the limits of a single excitation-or-inhibition mechanism.

references.title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound (tFUS) and Transcranial Unfocused Ultrasound (tUS) Neuromodulation: From Theoretical Principles to Stimulation Practices
references.authority: Lazzaro di Biase, Emma Falato, and Vincenzo Di Lazzaro; Frontiers in Neurology
references.notes: Review source for ultrasound neuromodulation physics, stimulation parameters, targeting, reported effects, safety considerations, and mechanism uncertainty.

references.title: Cochlear Implantation: An Overview
references.authority: Nicholas L. Deep, Eric M. Dowling, Daniel Jethanamest, and Matthew L. Carlson; Journal of Neurological Surgery Part B: Skull Base
references.version: Journal of Neurological Surgery Part B: Skull Base 80(2), 169–177 (2019); DOI 10.1055/s-0038-1669411
references.notes: Clinical overview supporting the cochlear-implant chain from acoustic input and signal processing to encoded electrical stimulation of surviving auditory neural elements.

references.title: Adaptive deep brain stimulation in advanced Parkinson disease
references.authority: Simon Little et al.; Annals of Neurology
references.notes: Primary human study demonstrating adaptive DBS in which a neural biomarker was used to control stimulation rather than applying one fixed stimulation command continuously.

references.title: Long-term treatment with responsive brain stimulation in adults with refractory partial seizures
references.authority: Gregory K. Bergey et al.; Neurology
references.notes: Long-term clinical evidence for responsive direct neurostimulation that detects programmed electrocorticographic patterns and delivers stimulation to seizure foci.

references.title: Long-term wireless streaming of neural recordings for circuit discovery and adaptive stimulation in individuals with Parkinson's disease
references.authority: Ro'ee Gilron et al.; Nature Biotechnology
references.notes: Human chronic neural-streaming study linking individualized biomarkers with adaptive DBS and illustrating real-world sensing, decoding, and feedback constraints.

references.title: The Science of Neural Interface Systems
references.authority: Nicholas G. Hatsopoulos and John P. Donoghue; Annual Review of Neuroscience
references.notes: Review source for neural-interface systems, recording approaches, decoding, and the systems-level relationship between interface capability and application requirements.

references.title: Electrical stimulation of excitable tissue: design of efficacious and safe protocols
references.authority: Daniel R. Merrill, Marom Bikson, and John G. R. Jefferys; Journal of Neuroscience Methods
references.notes: Invited review supporting the separation of stimulation efficacy from safety and the dependence of charge injection and damage risk on electrodes, waveforms, materials, and tissue.

references.title: Response of brain tissue to chronically implanted neural electrodes
references.authority: Vadim S. Polikov, Patrick A. Tresco, and William M. Reichert; Journal of Neuroscience Methods
references.notes: Review source for acute and chronic tissue response to implanted neural electrodes and the implications of biological response for long-term interface performance.

references.title: A Materials Roadmap to Functional Neural Interface Design
references.authority: Steven M. Wellman et al.; Advanced Functional Materials
references.notes: Review and design-roadmap source emphasizing interdependent material, tissue, channel-density, signal-access, and chronic-function tradeoffs in neural interfaces.

references.title: Failure mode analysis of silicon-based intracortical microelectrode arrays in non-human primates
references.authority: James C. Barrese et al.; Journal of Neural Engineering
references.notes: Primary chronic-array study supporting the distinction between acute interface performance and long-term useful stability across biological, material, mechanical, and unknown failure modes.
